notes: ACCESS: Tier (a) HTTP-first worked throughout, no browser needed. robots.txt (Shopify default) has no Claude/Anthropic-bot disallow and no blanket Disallow:/ - all tiers permitted; used tier (a) curl fetches plus one Playwright (tier b) pass only to surface the Constructor.io XHR endpoint used by the client-rendered product grid, then switched back to direct HTTP calls against that same JSON API (ac.cnstrc.com/browse/group_id/<handle>) for all further verification, so effectively tier (a) end-to-end. TREE: built from union of (1) mega-menu drawer JSON embedded in the homepage HTML (data-menu-json blocks) - only 'Lifestyle > Home' (Water Bottles, Candles, Mugs, Home Decor, Entertaining) and 'Lifestyle > Sleep & Loungewear' (Pajamas, Robes, Socks & Slippers) touch home/textile-adjacent territory - and (2) the full /a/sitemaps/sitemap_collections_1.xml (7083 collection URLs) grep'd for every textile/storage keyword from both rule files (bedding, duvet, sheet, pillow, cushion, throw, blanket, curtain, rug, towel, tablecloth, napkin, linen, mattress, robe, storage, organiz, basket, closet, wardrobe, laundry, hamper, shelv, rack, drawer, caddy, crate, bin, tote). Indigo.ca is a bookstore first; it has no dedicated Bedding/Curtains/Rugs/Storage-Boxes/Organizers category anywhere in nav or sitemap. QTY/verification: for every keyword-matched candidate collection, fetched the page and pulled the Shopify collection object (id/handle/title/rule) plus, where the grid is Constructor.io-rendered (client-side, no SSR count), called the site's own ac.cnstrc.com/browse/group_id/<handle> JSON endpoint directly (same call the page's own JS makes) to read total_num_results and the Type/Category facet breakdown as evidence. EXCLUDED and why: /collections/organizing-storage ('Organizing & Storage', 1334 items) and /collections/organizing (2 items) both LOOK like a Storage category by title but the facet breakdown (Book Format: Kobo eBook/Paperback/Hardcover/Audiobook) and sampled product titles (e.g. 'How to Keep House While Drowning', 'The Laundry Book', 'Goodbye, Things: The New Japanese Minimalism') prove these are BOOK genre collections about organizing/decluttering, not physical storage products - excluded as books/media per brief scope. /collections/robes (2 items) sampled as 'Ballet Cardigan' x2 - apparel, not bathrobes/home textile - excluded. /collections/tofino-towel-co and /collections/towel-to-go (brand/vendor auto-collections for towel vendors) both currently show total_num_results=0 (empty, no live inventory) - excluded. /collections/kids-mealtime-food-storage (27 items) sampled as lunch bags, water bottles, popsicle moulds, bento boxes - kids mealtime/tableware, not home storage per storage.md Sec13 boundary - excluded. /collections/christmas-pillows-throws (live h1 'Pillows & Throws', which would otherwise be the correct dedicated Textile URL for throw pillows/blankets) currently returns total_num_results=0 - empty, no rows to record. /collections/home-decor (74 items) and /collections/home-entertaining (400 items) are broad mixed decor/kitchen catch-all collections whose own Type facet shows small counts of genuinely textile items (Pillows 12+11, Blankets 5+2, Napkins 4) scattered among non-textile/non-storage items (candles, mugs, vases, lighting, glassware, cutting boards) with no dedicated clean subcategory URL isolating just the textile items (only a query-string facet filter exists, which both rule files exclude as a non-standard/search-style URL) - so no valid leaf could be recorded without either conflating categories or fabricating a filter URL; skipped per rule. Net result: Indigo.ca currently has zero navigable, non-empty, dedicated Textile or Storage category/subcategory listing pages - textile_rows and storage_rows are both correctly empty, not a research gap.
